title: Degree of topological categoricity of Baire space
formal: Does Baire space \(\omega^\omega\) have a least Turing degree relative to which every pair of its computable presentations admits a computable homeomorphism?
definitions: Definitions and model details remain incomplete. Define presentation and relative computability of homeomorphisms; existence of a least degree is the main target, with its identification a further source question.

import_provenance.original_title: The degree of topological categoricity of Baire space
import_provenance.original_statement: Is there a least Turing degree d such that every two computable presentations of Baire space omega^omega admit a d-computable homeomorphism? If such a degree exists, identify it.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: The maps are homeomorphisms rather than isometries; this is the topological categoricity problem stated by Ng, not ordinary categoricity of a discrete structure.

source_spot_check.finding: Section 8, Problem 28 asks whether Baire space has a degree of categoricity; no isometry substitution.
